review_notes: Read the whole file, focusing on proofs sharing machinery: partialSups_disjointed, Fintype.sup_disjointed, disjointed_partialSups, disjointed_succ, Monotone.disjointed_succ_sup. Grepped Mathlib for an existing lemma on `biUnion Iic` and found none for the Iio case (only IsLUB.biUnion_Iic_eq_Iio in Order/Interval/Set/Disjoint.lean, which is about sets and a different statement). I could not compile anything, so the proposed rewrites are sketches. The exact goal shape after `congr 2 with r` in disjointed_partialSups is uncertain. The univ variant in Fintype.sup_disjointed is trivial and I did not count it as repeated reasoning. The two findings are small and similar in scale.

findings.problem: The non-maximal case redoes the work of `disjointed_succ` and `Monotone.disjointed_succ`, which sit directly above in the same section. It unfolds `disjointed`, proves `Iio (succ i) = Iic i`, turns the sup over `Iic i` into `partialSups f i`, and rewrites with `hf.partialSups_eq`. `disjointed_succ` proves the same identification via `congr 2 with m` and `lt_succ_iff_of_not_isMax`, and `Monotone.disjointed_succ` already gives `disjointed f (succ i) = f (succ i) \ f i`.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the `rw [disjointed_apply] … sdiff_sup_cancel` block of the `¬IsMax` branch with a use of the existing lemma: `· rw [hf.disjointed_succ h, sdiff_sup_cancel (hf (le_succ i))]`. The `IsMax` branch stays as is. This removes the local `Iio (succ i) = Iic i` argument and the `partialSups_apply` round trip. It is untested, and `le_succ` is the `Order.le_succ` already used in `sup_Ioc_disjointed_of_monotone`.
findings.benefit: The `Iio (succ i) = Iic i` argument then lives only in `disjointed_succ`. The lemma becomes a two-line consequence of the successor API, so a change to `disjointed` needs only one place updated.

have hun : (Iio i).biUnion Iic = Iio i := by
      ext r; simpa using ⟨fun ⟨a, ha⟩ ↦ ha.2.trans_lt ha.1, fun hr ↦ ⟨r, hr, le_rfl⟩⟩
findings.problem: The fact `(Iio i).biUnion Iic = Iio i` is proved twice with the same witness pair. `partialSups_disjointed` proves it as `hun` (lines 139-140). `disjointed_partialSups` re-proves it inline (lines 176-178) after `congr 2 with r`. In both, `Iio i` is a lower set and each `r` is in `Iic r`. Both proofs also use the same `sup_biUnion` strategy to convert `(Iio i).sup` into a sup of `partialSups`. `Fintype.sup_disjointed` has a third, easier variant of it for `univ`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a private lemma before `partialSups_disjointed`: `private lemma biUnion_Iic_Iio (i : ι) : (Iio i).biUnion Iic = Iio i`. Prove it with the current `ext r; simpa using ⟨fun ⟨a, ha⟩ ↦ ha.2.trans_lt ha.1, fun hr ↦ ⟨r, hr, le_rfl⟩⟩`. In `partialSups_disjointed`, use `rw [← biUnion_Iic_Iio i, …]` and `biUnion_Iic_Iio i` in the later `simp only [..., hun]`, replacing `hun`. In `disjointed_partialSups`, replace the final `congr 2 with r; simpa only [...]` with `rw [biUnion_Iic_Iio]`, or with `Finset.ext_iff.mp (biUnion_Iic_Iio i) r` if the goal is still membership-wise. This is untested, and the exact goal after `simp only [..., ← sup_biUnion]` may need a small adjustment. The new lemma needs `[PartialOrder ι] [LocallyFiniteOrderBot ι]` and `DecidableEq ι`, both already available in this section after `classical`.
findings.benefit: The lower-set argument is stated and proved once, with a name. Both main proofs read as 'rewrite the sup over `Iio i` as a sup of `partialSups`', without a re-derived membership argument in each. If the unfolding of `Iic` or `Iio` changes, only one proof needs fixing.
